title: Protocol for Assessing Neighborhood Physical Disorder Using YOLOv8 Deep Learning Model
author: Li, Ma, et al.

steps.title: Acquire street view images
steps.instruction: Collect street‑view imagery for the study area using commercial APIs and/or self‑recorded captures, ensuring full spatial coverage.

substeps.instruction: Download images from Google Street View (covers 100 countries across North and South America, Europe, and Oceania).
For China, obtain images from Baidu Street View (currently active) and note that Tencent Street View stopped updates in 2015.

If commercial coverage is missing for any location or time period, perform self‑organized data collection by driving a vehicle equipped with a camera to scan the target streets; the acquisition time depends on the area size.

steps.title: Assemble training dataset
steps.instruction: Combine the downloaded commercial images with the self‑collected images to create a unified dataset for model training.

substeps.instruction: Organize all images by geographic location and acquisition date.
Retain the original image metadata (e.g., GPS coordinates, timestamp) for later spatial and temporal analysis.

steps.title: Train YOLOv8 recognition model
steps.instruction: Use the assembled image set to train a YOLOv8 deep‑learning model that detects physical‑disorder features.

substeps.instruction: Configure the YOLOv8 architecture for object detection of disorder indicators (e.g., boarded‑up buildings, damaged façades, vacant lots, inadequate signage, litter).
Run training on the full dataset; computational time will vary with city size and image count.

steps.title: Compute physical disorder scores
steps.instruction: Apply the trained YOLOv8 model to all street‑view images to generate quantitative PD measurements at multiple spatial scales.

substeps.instruction: Run inference on each image to obtain disorder detections.
Aggregate detections to calculate PD indices for individual streets, neighborhoods, and the entire city (e.g., Xining City, China).
Record PD values with their associated timestamps to enable daily or monthly temporal resolution (as supported by the data).

steps.title: Analyze temporal PD changes
steps.instruction: Examine how physical‑disorder scores evolve over time across the study area.

substeps.instruction: Compare PD indices across successive time points (daily, monthly, or annually as available).
Identify trends, hotspots, or reductions in disorder and relate them to urban‑planning or policy interventions.

description: The actual time required for each computational step will largely depend on the scale of the studied city and the quantity of street views involved. The more city streets to analyze, the longer the time required. It is important to note that street view data can be purchased from several commercial companies through Application Processing Interfaces (APIs). Google Street View covers 100 countries across North and South America, Europe, and Oceania. In countries where it doesn’t provide coverage, alternative street view services are available. For instance, in China, Baidu currently conducts street view collection and continues to update, while Tencent Street View ceased updates and services in 2015. For areas or time periods not covered by commercial street views, a self-organized data collection method can be employed. The time frame for data acquisition will be determined by the time taken to scan specific areas using a vehicle. This article uses the city of Xining in China as an example to illustrate the time intervals for each step, including acquiring commercial street views and supplementing with self-collected data.
